director.chapterArc: A long, confessional monologue by Rook (Elias Marsh) revealing the history of Homura, Vera Kess, Satori, and his personal guilt regarding Cinder Company. The delivery must remain grounded in Toren's observational distance while allowing Rook's voice to carry the weight of trauma without melodrama.
director.restraintNote: The emotional peak is not a shout but a quiet admission of failure ('I did not keep it'). Maintain clinical precision during exposition; let silence do the heavy lifting after revelations. Do not rush the 'Satori' definition or the description of Vera's death.

cues.delivery: Establish the scene: a large fire in a ruined yard. Toren's observational tone is grounded and sensory-focused.
cues.from: Chapter 17 — Homura
cues.through: And out past the wall the dark had got much darker, the way it does.
cues.reason: Scene setting before Rook begins speaking.

cues.delivery: Rook's preparation. Flat affect, deliberate movements. He is setting a boundary for his story.
cues.from: Rook sat down on the flat stone with the fire between him and all of them, and pushed his left sleeve back, and undid the buckle.
cues.through: "Right. I'm going to do this in order, and I'd ask you to let me. If I go out of order I'll stop, and I do not think I would start again." He looked at the fire rather than at any of them. "It starts a long way from here and it takes a while to get to anything you'd recognize. Don't help me along."
cues.reason: Establishing Rook as the speaker with controlled authority.

cues.delivery: Exposition on Lowry Bend. Rook speaks flatly as information; no emotional coloring yet.
cues.from: "There's a village called Lowry Bend," he said. "It's about four hundred miles south-east of the rock cut, which means none of you have ever heard of it, and nor has anybody else.
cues.through: Milo laughed and stopped himself instantly.

cues.delivery: Rook's personal history of being 'late'. A matter-of-fact recounting of his mother and brothers.
cues.from: "No," Rook said. "You're right. That's what he was like. That's exactly what he was like."
cues.through: "Then it came?" said Milo.

cues.delivery: The story of being bought. Rook's voice remains flat; the horror is in the facts.
cues.from: "Then it came. In the eleventh month, in the dark, on the bridge with the hole in it, which is a whole other evening and not the one we're having." He shifted. "What matters about it is that it came through my mother's door, because that was the only door anybody in that place had ever heard of. I was a hand. Fourteen years old and a hand, and about a fifth as good at it as she was at twenty, and extremely pleased with myself."
cues.through: "For nine more years. She never used most of it. She kept giving her turns at the doctor away to other people's children, which is a thing I did not find out until it was much too late to have an argument with her about it."

cues.delivery: Introduction of Homura. The word 'fracture' is delivered with clinical precision.
cues.from: "The place they took me to was called Homura," Rook said.
cues.through: "You lived there?" said Wyck.

cues.delivery: Orrin Vell and the experiment. Rook describes the pairing method with detached observation.
cues.from: "Sixty of us. Forty were children." Rook put the thorn on the fire. "You do not study a thing by going and standing where it isn't."
cues.through: "Because on your own you'd explain it with your own words," she said slowly. "And your own words would fit. They'd always fit. So you'd never find out they were the wrong ones."

cues.delivery: The description of the valley life. Rook speaks with a hint of nostalgia but keeps it flat.
cues.from: "Yes." Rook nodded once. "You cannot get outside your own tradition by thinking hard. You can only get outside it by being tied at the wrist to somebody whose tradition is different and who is as sure as you are."
cues.through: The fire cracked. Nobody moved at all.

cues.delivery: Introduction of Vera Kess. Rook's tone shifts slightly to acknowledge the conflict between them.
cues.from: "She was a year older than me. Stone clan — eight generations of it, up on the north side of the Marches, one of the old ones that had kept more of its own vocabulary than most clans bother to. That matters. Remember that she had words nobody else had.
cues.through: He stopped.

cues.delivery: The raid and Vera's death. Rook pauses significantly before 'She lived'. The delivery is heavy with guilt but restrained.
cues.from: It was the first time he had stopped since he started, and Toren, on the other side of a fire, watched a man take a breath the way a person takes a step onto a floor they are not sure of.
cues.through: "And then?" said Toren.
cues.reason: Climax of the backstory; requires emotional weight without melodrama.

cues.delivery: The definition of Satori. Rook speaks with absolute clarity; the concept is delivered as a revelation.
cues.from: He had not meant to speak.
cues.through: Wyck said it too. Toren heard his own voice go with theirs about a half-beat late, and afterward he could never work out whether it had been a strange thing to do or the only available thing.

cues.delivery: The mechanics of Satori. Rook explains 'empty mind' and 'open soul'. Flat delivery to emphasize the logic.
cues.from: "Right," Rook said. "I have thought about how to say this part for eleven years and have never once had to do it out loud. So it will come out poorly, and you're going to have it poorly.
cues.through: "You did it," Rook said.

cues.delivery: Dessa's realization. Rook is direct and unsoftened; he confirms the truth of her experience.
cues.from: "Four seconds," said Dessa.
cues.through: "Vell believed her. That's the thing about him. A sixteen-year-old girl with a bad shoulder told a man who had been right about everything for thirty years that the foundation of all nine traditions was a misunderstanding, and he listened to her for two hours and then went and changed the entire program.

cues.delivery: The results of the experiment. Rook speaks with a sense of lost potential; 'Identical' is delivered as a fact.
cues.from: "After that it was one question. Do nine traditions measure the same, or don't they.
cues.through: "It was going to end the oldest argument in the world with a column of numbers."

cues.delivery: The raid by Cinder Company. Rook's voice drops; the description of 'three men' is delivered with cold precision.
cues.from: "And on the eleventh of the ninth month," Rook said, "Cinder Company came over the wire."
cues.through: His voice came out wrong.

cues.delivery: Toren's realization. Rook confirms 'I recognized it'. The delivery is stark.
cues.from: "No," said Rook.
cues.through: "They came for the records," Rook said. "That is the whole of what they were there for. They killed the people who got in the way of the records. They killed a number who didn't. And they took every sheet of paper in that valley, and both instrument benches, and the ledgers back to the first year.

cues.delivery: The aftermath of the raid. Rook lists the dead and survivors with a flat, factual tone.
cues.from: "Forty-nine people out of sixty.
cues.through: "I got to her," Rook said. "That is the one piece of luck in the whole of that night and I have never once been able to decide what it was worth. I had about four minutes.

cues.delivery: The promise and the Ember strap. Rook handles the object with reverence; his voice is quiet.
cues.from: "And what she spent them on was making me promise to get the papers out."
cues.through: "I took it off the floor of the room she died in. It was nine feet from her and the strap had come off it. I picked it up because I was nineteen and I could not leave it lying on a floor.

cues.delivery: The strap doesn't fit. Rook admits this with a sense of finality and relief.
cues.from: "I have worn it every day since. Eleven years." He turned it over once. "And it does not fit me. It has never fitted me and it is not going to. Every single one of you has looked at that strap at some point in four weeks and thought that's odd."
cues.through: Toren looked round the fire.

cues.delivery: The group's reaction. Rook turns back to them; the atmosphere is heavy.
cues.from: Milo was crying without making any noise about it, which he had got very good at. Dessa had not moved at all. Senna was sitting up with her hands folded and her chin level, looking at the man's back with an expression Toren had seen on her exactly once before, on a gray morning in a doorway at Hobb's Wall.
cues.through: Dessa put her hand flat over her own left forearm, above the wrist, where the strap had been.

cues.delivery: The connection between the strap and Dessa. Rook explains why he gave it to her.
cues.from: "You went and stood in the water," she said.
cues.through: Wyck said, very quietly, "No."

cues.delivery: The second tragedy. Rook describes his mother's death with a flat tone; the horror is in the lack of emotion.
cues.from: "Yes," said Rook.
cues.through: "And here is the thing you will not believe.

cues.delivery: The realization of the company's name. Rook speaks slowly; the connection is made.
cues.from: "For years I did not put it together."
cues.through: He held it up between two fingers, small and square with the corners taken off, and the firelight found it. Toren, nine feet away, could see the chevron with the line struck through it, cut poorly, off center, by somebody in a hurry a long time ago.

cues.delivery: The chit and the company. Rook holds up the object; his voice is steady.
cues.from: "I had been looking at that mark for four days on a cliff road while nine competent men worked above my village," Rook said. "And I had been looking at it in a valley at two in the morning when I was nineteen, on the shoulder of a man going past me in the dark with an instrument bench on his back. I had not known I had looked at it until a bootmaker turned one over on a counter six years later.
cues.through: Senna said, "Hm."

pauses.after: And out past the wall the dark had got much darker, the way it does.
pauses.reason: Scene reset after establishing the fire and visibility.

pauses.after: "Right. I'm going to do this in order, and I'd ask you to let me. If I go out of order I'll stop, and I do not think I would start again." He looked at the fire rather than at any of them. "It starts a long way from here and it takes a while to get to anything you'd recognize. Don't help me along."
pauses.reason: Pause for Rook's instruction to let him speak in order.

pauses.after: "I was bought," he said. "That is the plain word. I have never found a better one, and I have had eleven years to look. And I would have gone anyway. She knew I would have gone anyway. Neither of us ever said so."
pauses.reason: Heavy pause after 'I was bought' and the admission of going anyway.

pauses.after: "And it was built on purpose, on a fracture."
pauses.reason: Major landing on 'built on purpose, on a fracture'. Allow the concept to sink in.

pauses.after: "And it was the best place I have ever been in my life."
pauses.reason: Pause after Rook calls it the best place he's ever been; contrast with the coldness described before.
Short pause to isolate 'Vera was in that shed' as a pivot point.

pauses.after: "I was fifteen. That's the number I'd like you all to have. Fifteen, with my mother's hands on the end of my arms, standing in a corridor."
pauses.reason: Major landing on the number fifteen and Rook's paralysis. Allow the weight of his guilt to land.
Isolating the age to emphasize Rook's paralysis and guilt.

pauses.after: Wyck said it too. Toren heard his own voice go with theirs about a half-beat late, and afterward he could never work out whether it had been a strange thing to do or the only available thing.
pauses.reason: Pause after the group says 'Satori' together; let the word resonate.
Pause after 'Identical'; emphasize the finality of the scientific proof.
Emphasis on the absolute nature of the Homura findings.

pauses.after: Three men stood across the gate and did not move. Everybody else was moving. Why would you put three men on an open gate you had already come through.
pauses.reason: Major landing on Toren's realization about the gate. The shift from hillside to memory requires a beat.

pauses.before: Three men stood across the gate and did not move.
pauses.reason: Preparation for Toren's internal visualization of the raid tactic.
Pause after 'I recognized it'; Rook admits his knowledge was hidden.
Emphasis on the scale of loss at Homura.

pauses.after: It sat narrow and neat against the inside of a grown man's arm like a coin in a purse made for a smaller coin.
pauses.reason: Major landing on the description of the strap fitting a girl. The visual contrast is crucial.

pauses.before: There is one other way to answer for it
pauses.reason: Preparation for Rook's shift from vengeance to teaching.
Major landing on 'Because I was asleep'. This is the heaviest line; allow silence to follow.
